reason: Could not break it. I downloaded the 1929 Knopf Jade Mountain scan and read the leaf: under the running head THE JADE MOUNTAIN, after ON A MOONLIGHT NIGHT, stands A SPRING VIEW, and its opening four lines are Though a country be sundered, hills and rivers endure; / And spring comes green again to trees and grasses / Where petals have been shed like tears / And lonely birds have sung their grief. That is the shipped text word for word and break for break, semicolon after endure, capitals at And, Where and And as the edition sets them. The page: the footer on that leaf OCRs as 48, but the book's index of first lines carries Though a country be sundered, hills and rivers endure 148, and the leaf takes the even-page running head (the book title, with the poet's name on odd pages), so 148 is right and the OCR simply lost the leading 1. shipped.js: nothing shipped and nothing near, under Du Fu and again under Tu Fu, 0 of 3, not banned. Source line 109 characters, leads with the name, no em dash (the only hyphen is inside Kang-hu), ends in a full stop, curly quotes only. Poetry is the form; an eighth-century poem in a 1929 translation is in scope; the grief here is petals and birds, so no content warning is owed; and a country sundered while hills and rivers endure is the month's theme in one line. Two things the editor should see, neither of them a refutation. First, the 1929 title page credits the work to Witter Bynner from the texts of Kiang Kang-hu, which the source line compresses to with Kiang Kang-hu: defensible, but carry-in 04-poet-08 renders the same book as trans. Witter Bynner, 1929, so the month would print two forms of one credit unless the editor picks one. Second, and more serious for the calendar than for this card: carry-in 04-poet-08 (Li Bai, The Hard Road, The Jade Mountain, p. 70) is marked fitMonth 8 and its own note says only one Bynner may stand in a month. August cannot take both, so one of the two has to move.
